To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Deep Learning can be used for ontology learning from the biomedical literature; Deep Learning outperformed LSA, LSA outperformed LDA and LDA outperformed CBOW and Skipgram; and, LSA, LDC, CBOW and Skigram performed better with larger corpus.
Deep Learning can be used to learn word embeddings for ontology engineering from the literature and that Deep Learning outperforms traditional DSMs for ontology learning from biomedical corpora.

1. Deep Learning can contribute significantly to ontology engineering from biomedical text, 2. The performance of Deep Learning models is comparable with LSA and LDA, 3. Deep Learning models are more robust to the size of the corpus used.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following: 1) The use of Deep Learning for ontology learning; 2) The use of PubMed for ontology learning; and 3) The use of the patient safety domain for ontology learning.
the following questions: How to use Deep Learning to learn ontologies? How to evaluate the quality of learned ontologies? How does Deep Learning compare to traditional methods?

the following: (1) the development of a methodology to derive word embeddings from PubMed using Deep Learning; (2) a comparison between the results obtained with LDA, LSA, CBOW and skip-gram; (3) a comparison between word embeddings derived using 300K PubMed titles and abstract and those derived using 14M titles and abstracts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Deep Learning models can be successfully used in the ontology engineering task.
Deep Learning is a promising approach for ontology learning, but further work needs to be conducted to improve its performance.

(1) Deep Learning methods are better than the traditional methods for ontology engineering; (2) the performance of the Deep Learning models depends on the size of the corpus, and (3) the performance of Deep Learning models is not affected by the size of the ontology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Deep Learning can provide an effective solution to the ontology engineering problem.
the use of Deep Learning in ontology engineering can be a viable alternative, and in some cases, a more efficient alternative to traditional methods.
Deep Learning models are able to outperform traditional DSMs for biomedical ontology learning.
The main takeaway from our work is that
Deep Learning can outperform traditional DSMs when the size of the training corpus is increased.
, in order to obtain the best performance, we should consider the use of Deep Learning models in conjunction with traditional distributional semantic models.
the application of neural networks to derive word embeddings can be used to improve biomedical knowledge representation.
